service: Sign in with Apple (Apple ID OAuth 2.0 / OIDC)

token_exchange_response.description: Returned by POST https://appleid.apple.com/auth/token upon authorization_code exchange.

id_token_decoded_jwt_claims.description: Decoded claims from the Apple id_token JWT. IMPORTANT: Apple only sends the user's name and email on the FIRST login — your backend MUST persist them immediately.

fields_explained.sub: Unique, stable, team-scoped Apple user ID (e.g., '001234.abc567def890.1234'). This is your primary identifier.
fields_explained.email: User email (may be a Private Relay address like 'abc123@privaterelay.appleid.com')
fields_explained.email_verified: Whether Apple has verified this email (string 'true'/'false', NOT a boolean)
fields_explained.is_private_email: Whether the email is an Apple Private Relay forwarding address (string 'true'/'false')
fields_explained.real_user_status: 0 = unsupported, 1 = unknown, 2 = likely real (anti-fraud signal, first login only)
fields_explained.nonce_supported: Whether the nonce claim was included in the authorization request

data_types.aud: string (your Apple Services ID / Client ID)
data_types.sub: string (unique, stable, pairwise team-scoped Apple User ID)

first_login_authorization_callback.description: Apple sends the user's name ONLY on the very first authorization via the form_post callback body. You must capture and store it immediately — Apple will NEVER send it again.

data_types.code: string (single-use authorization code for token exchange)
data_types.user: string (JSON-encoded string containing firstName, lastName, and email; sent ONCE only)

payload.error_description: The code has expired or has been revoked.
